# Offense — Offense Security

Offense is the first product from Offense Security. Canonical home: https://offense.sh.
One account and one API key give a coding agent access to enabled hosted security
tools, with prepaid per-tool pricing. Basic npm/pnpm dependency advisory audits
remain free and need no account or model key.

## Set up your agent

Read the maintained skill and client installation reference. Install only in the
requested project scope, preserve customizations and inspect helpers before
execution. Installation does not authorize scans, purchases or application edits.

- Skill: https://offense.sh/skills/offense/SKILL.md
- Installation: https://offense.sh/skills/offense/references/install.md
- CLI/tool workflow: https://offense.sh/skills/offense/references/tools.md
- Existing local tools and optional helpers: https://offense.sh/skills/offense/references/local-tools.md
- Agent console and setup: https://offense.sh/app
- Installation guide: https://offense.sh/skill
- API key portal: https://offense.sh/account#keys
- Prepaid balance and billing: https://offense.sh/account#billing

The helper bundle includes scripts/cli.mjs. Device login opens a first-party
browser page; the human checks the comparison code and approves the account.
The key is received once and stored privately by the CLI, never in project MCP
configuration. Alternatively, the user can create a key in the first-party API
key portal and configure it privately through the documented CLI/environment
workflow. Do not ask for a key in chat or put it in project files. No GitHub App
installation, repository connection, Cloudflare connection or OpenRouter key is
required for the core tool workflow. Optional cloud tools require their own
explicitly selected account scope. Offense tools work alongside the agent's
existing local tools; Offense does not replace the agent or its model.

After installing a skill or MCP configuration, start a new coding-agent session.
Use the CLI immediately while a new session is pending. Preserve native project
trust and tool permissions; report provider safeguard blocks accurately.

## Human CLI

Node20+ is required. The npm-compatible client archive is available without an
npm-registry publication:

npm install --global https://offense.sh/downloads/offense-cli.tgz
offense login
offense tools
offense balance
offense topup
offense mcp install --client codex --project .

The standalone file is https://offense.sh/downloads/offense-cli.mjs and its SHA256
manifest is https://offense.sh/downloads/offense-cli-manifest.json.

## API and MCP

- Public tool directory (no sign-in): https://offense.sh/tools
- Tool coverage, upstream source and usage: https://offense.sh/tools/<tool-id>
- Public catalog with availability and prices: https://offense.sh/v1/catalog
- Authenticated catalog: GET https://offense.sh/v1/tools
- Account: GET https://offense.sh/v1/account
- Quote: POST https://offense.sh/v1/quotes
- Tool call: POST https://offense.sh/v1/call/<tool-id>
- Asynchronous job/result: /v1/scans and /v1/scans/<id>
- Usage and balance: GET https://offense.sh/v1/usage
- Whop top-up link: POST https://offense.sh/v1/billing/topups with an empty object
- Hosted MCP: https://offense.sh/mcp

Use one Bearer Offense API key for hosted tools. Inspect a quote and set an
explicit maximum charge before a paid call. Idempotency keys prevent duplicate
jobs/charges; preserve the same key and input when recovering uncertain outcomes.
Whop handles payment approval. A browser return does not grant funds; verified
payment readback and the durable ledger credit purchases once.

The authenticated CLI MCP proxy exposes catalog, quote, call, result, account and
top-up capabilities. Anonymous native HTTP MCP retains the free
`offense.audit_dependencies` capability. The current agent keeps repository
connections, applicability review, edits and tests. Findings are review signals,
not confirmed exploitable vulnerabilities.

Old app.purpleteam.sh endpoints, account identities, balances, keys and advanced
/skills/purple resources remain compatibility aliases. New public branding is
Offense and Offense Security. The community repository remains private.
